verdicts.idea: Implement Advanced Context Engineering for Claude Code
verdicts.reason: The proposal's substance (structured agent context) is CLAUDE.md + `knowledge/` + path-scoped `.claude/rules/` + 30+ skills + the persistent memory system + `/work-on` preloading — maintained daily by the wrap-up rituals.

verdicts.idea: Develop an AI-Driven Financial Audit Agent (Shadow Ledger)
verdicts.reason: The repo's audit layer (DQ checks, reconciliations, pre-flight, QA) and AI-narrative half (weekly BI report, digest synthesis) already exist, with a grounding gate for AI narratives.
The concrete, local version of this idea (staged-script handoff, classifier-allowlist decision) is already tracked by #1902, making a generic 'async orchestration' project redundant.
This repo's only cryptography is own-secret handling, and no LLM call site or tool exposes decryption capabilities to agents, making the attack shape absent.
This is the only genuinely open idea, with no deadline, and is naturally #1418-adjacent.
The PR Review Gate already runs an Opus pass and Copilot shadow lane for code review and issue triage.

verdicts.idea: Upgrade to Opus 5 & develop Claude Skills
verdicts.reason: Opus 5 is already the top model in CLAUDE.md, and there are already 25 skills in `.claude/skills/` with a rule to promote recurring operations to skills.

verdicts.idea: Harden AI agent security with Cloud Run sandboxes
verdicts.reason: Cloud Run sandboxes are for untrusted code, but crumbl-ops runs its own deterministic jobs and already has other security measures like deny-all egress and scoped service accounts.

verdicts.idea: Optimize Gemini / hybrid LLM for finance
verdicts.reason: Invoice parsing has never involved an LLM; it is deterministic per-vendor code, and a hybrid local-LLM strategy is enterprise ML-ops for a small operation.

All named components like AI test generation, property-based testing, mutation testing, forecast backtesting, model drift detection, and anomaly detection already exist, and LightGBM models were deleted in 2026-05.

verdicts.idea: Fortify AI Agent Security and Access
verdicts.reason: Harden-runner egress-policy, `src/ops/secret_redaction.py`, and repo-wide `system_instruction` rules ensure robust security.
24 skills in `.claude/skills/`, the manifest-driven weekly-review harness, and `CLAUDE.md` are already implemented.
Data and alarms exist in `src/ops/llm_metrics.py`, with only a consolidated dollar cost-per-purpose rollup missing, which is a reporting convenience.
This is `project_qa_framework`, including property tests, mutation testing, and adversarial multi-agent review.

The premise is false as no LLM extraction exists to validate; existing deterministic parsers are already covered by corpus-validation-before-goldens with live dollar-level backstops such as dup-bill DQ (#991), vendor-draft bank-rec (#987), check_required_qbo_vendors (#848), and suspense-JE for unbalanced posts.
CLAUDE.md §Model Selection, refreshed in #882, already covers model selection and subagent tiering, making an internal LLM gateway over-engineering at the current 2-owner scale.
Current practice, including 20+ skills, hooks, headless cron sessions (`claude -p`), and dual-model weekly review, already surpasses the proposed script harness for generating unit tests.

`src/ops/llm_metrics.py`, CS classifier observability (migration 152), LLM-related DQ checks (`data_quality/system.py`), Gemini output-cap tripwires, and the weekly-review metrics ledger already provide appropriate scale observability.
CLAUDE.md was refreshed with Fable guidance, escalation categories, and subagent tiering, though the full 'model-picker system' was deemed over-engineering.

verdicts.idea: Autoresearch Loops for AI Model Validation
verdicts.reason: The repo already contains the proposed machinery for LLM release gates, but the digest's premises about LightGBM and Gemini invoice extraction were incorrect.
The repo already incorporates action-tier gates, persist-gates, dedup tags, suspense-JE holds, deploy point-of-action approval, and PreToolUse hooks.
The proposed elements of skills/, subagents, workflows, knowledge/, and memory already form the project's operating model.
